ai.title: Add o3 and o4-mini models to Freebuff
ai.summary: Added `o3-2025-04-16` and `o4-mini-2025-04-16` to `openaiModels` in `common/src/constants.ts`. Updated `shortModelNames` and `providerModelNames` mappings to expose these models to the CLI picker and backend. `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts` includes new token cost entries for input, output, and cache-read.

eli5.text: You can now pick two newer AI helpers, o3 and o4-mini, when choosing a model for your chat. The system now recognizes these two new options in its model list and tracks how much they cost per task, so when you use them your account is billed at their specific rates. This change is live today, and image uploads are already rejected for these models along with the other related tweaks in the same release.

ai.title: Extend image content rejection to o3 and o4-mini
ai.summary: The `transformMessages` function in `backend/src/llm-apis/openai-api.ts` now applies the image content rejection logic to `openaiModels.o3` and `openaiModels.o4mini` alongside `openaiModels.o3mini`. This prevents these models from receiving image inputs, which they do not support, avoiding upstream errors. The change is scoped to the backend LLM API adapter.

eli5.text: Starting today, the system now blocks image-based messages from being sent to the newest generation of language models, including o3 and o4-mini, which were previously allowed through. If you try to include an image in a request that uses one of these models, it will be rejected earlier in the process instead of causing a failure later. Only requests using these specific models are affected; other models continue to handle images as before.

ai.title: Simplify endturn prompt in main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: The `end_turn` instruction in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` was simplified by removing the conditional `isGPT4_1` check. The core rule for emitting `<end_turn></end_turn>` now applies uniformly, with the multi-part completion directive moved into the main instruction block. This change affects the backend's main prompt generation logic.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes instructions that tell our AI how to respond got a small tidy-up. Instead of having a special rule only for certain AI models, the guidance about when to wrap up a response now works the same way for all of them, and the note about finishing multi-part tasks was moved into the main set of directions. Nothing changes for you right now, but this kind of cleanup helps keep the AI's behavior consistent.

ai.title: Allow slash-prefixed help command in CLI
ai.summary: CLI `processCommand` now accepts `/help` alongside `help` and `h`. This aligns command parsing with common slash-command conventions. Change scoped to `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: The command-line assistant now recognizes the typed command /help in addition to the previous help and h shortcuts to display the help menu. If you use the command-line version of the assistant, typing /help will now bring up the help list just like the other two shortcuts. The change is live today in the command-line application.

ai.title: Remove email link from referrals page
ai.summary: Referrals page now displays referrer name as plain text, removing mailto link. Eliminates next/link import and Button wrapper. Updates web/src/app/referrals/page.tsx.

eli5.text: When you visit your referral page, the name of the person who invited you now appears as plain text instead of a clickable email link. This means tapping the name will no longer open your email app to send them a message. The change affects anyone viewing their referrals page and is live today.

ai.title: Referral code application on login
ai.summary: Web referral flow applies codes on login. `web/src/app/api/referrals/route.ts` handles both web sessions and CLI tokens. `web/src/app/page.tsx` and `sign-in-button.tsx` store `referral_code` in `localStorage` pre-auth, triggering redemption post-login. `referrals/[code]/page.tsx` key renamed from `codebuff_referral_code` to `referral_code`.

eli5.text: When you click a referral link and then log in, the system now correctly applies the referral code to give credit to whoever sent you there. If you're logged in via the website, the code is sent right after login; if you're logging in through the CLI (command-line tool), the code is saved temporarily and applied after sign-in. The referral tracking key was also renamed for consistency, so referral data is stored under a simpler name. This is live today and affects anyone using referral links to sign up, whether on the web or via CLI.

ai.title: Revert referral credits bonus to 250
ai.summary: Reverted CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS from 500 to 250 in common/src/constants.ts. This undoes a temporary increase in referral credits. The change affects the core constants used across the application.

eli5.text: The extra referral credit that was temporarily given earlier has now been taken back, so new referrals earn 250 credits instead of the 500 they did for a short time. This affects anyone who signs up using a referral link, since the credit is set in one shared place that the site reads from every time. If you looked today, you'd see 250 listed where 500 showed up before.

ai.title: Cancel response role user
ai.summary: npm-app/src/client.ts changes cancelled response role from assistant to user. Content now prepends Received output: to response buffer. Aligns cancelled turn with user message state.

eli5.text: When you cancel a response midway, it now appears in the app as a message you sent rather than a message the assistant sent. If you were watching the conversation, you'd notice the cancelled reply labeled as 'Received output:' under your own messages instead of under the assistant's messages. This helps keep the flow of the conversation aligned with who should be talking next.

ai.title: Enforce endturn tool call on response completion
ai.summary: Agent instructions and tool definitions now mandate `<end_turn></end_turn>` as a standalone final tool call whenever the assistant completes a response or awaits user input. The `end_turn` tool description in `backend/src/tools.ts` was updated to remove the previous constraint against combining it with other tool calls, instead requiring it to be the sole tool call in the final message. This change applies to the backend system prompt (`backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md`) and tool registry.

eli5.text: The assistant has always been supposed to signal the end of its reply with a special tag, but the old rule said it couldn't do that at the same time as any other action it takes. Now the instructions and the rulebook for that tag were rewritten so the assistant simply has to close every reply with that tag by itself, with no other actions bundled in. You wouldn't see a difference in what the assistant says, but if you peeked at how it's told to behave, the messy 'do not combine' restriction is gone and it now just ends each turn with the tag as required.

ai.title: Fix OpenAI stream usage parsing
ai.summary: OpenAI stream usage parsing now correctly separates cached tokens from total input tokens. `stream_options.include_usage` is set to true to enable usage data in the final chunk. `cached_tokens` are subtracted from `inputTokens` and stored in `cacheReadInputTokens`.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads from a conversation it has seen before, those already-read words are now counted separately from new words you actually type. You will see two numbers in the usage report instead of one merged total: how much was freshly written by you, and how much came straight from memory. This applies to streaming responses through the assistant's backend today.
